proposals.before: Returning, he saw many bones beside Jiyin city and wrote the provinces and commanderies to collect and bury them all.
proposals.after: Returning, he saw many bones beside Ji commandery's city and wrote the provinces and commanderies to collect and bury them all.
proposals.reason: Chinese 汲郡 is Ji commandery, not Jiyin (濟陰).

proposals.before: On his return he saw many bones beside Jiyin city and sent letters to the provinces and commanderies ordering all collected and buried.
proposals.after: On his return he saw many bones beside Ji commandery's city and sent letters to the provinces and commanderies ordering all collected and buried.
proposals.reason: Chinese 汲郡 is Ji commandery, not Jiyin (濟陰).

proposals.before: Emperor Xianzong summoned both and told Shigui: "I know the Terrace has long deceived the Court; hold to principle against them—keep this heart and you need not fear missing wealth and honor."
proposals.after: Emperor Xianzu summoned both and told Shigui: "I know the Terrace has long deceived the Court; hold to principle against them—keep this heart and you need not fear missing wealth and honor."
proposals.reason: Chinese 顯祖 is temple name Xianzu, not Xianzong.

proposals.before: Emperor Xianzong summoned the two men and in person charged Shigui: "I know the Terrace has long deceived the Court; you can hold to principle and contend with them—only keep this heart and do not worry that you will not be rich and honored."
proposals.after: Emperor Xianzu summoned the two men and in person charged Shigui: "I know the Terrace has long deceived the Court; you can hold to principle and contend with them—only keep this heart and do not worry that you will not be rich and honored."
proposals.reason: Chinese 顯祖 is temple name Xianzu, not Xianzong.

proposals.before: His father Wenyue had been administrator of Julu.
proposals.after: His father Wenye had been administrator of Julu.
proposals.reason: Chinese 文業 is Wenye, not Wenyue.

proposals.before: His father Wenyue was administrator of Julu.
proposals.after: His father Wenye was administrator of Julu.
proposals.reason: Chinese 文業 is Wenye, not Wenyue.

proposals.before: His father Bei served Wei as far as vice minister of the court of the imperial clan.
proposals.after: His father Bei served Wei as far as junior chamberlain for the palace guards.
proposals.reason: 衛尉少卿 is an office of the guards (衛尉), not the imperial clan court (宗正).

proposals.before: His father Bei served Wei up to vice minister of the court of the imperial clan.
proposals.after: His father Bei served Wei up to junior chamberlain for the palace guards.
proposals.reason: 衛尉少卿 is an office of the guards (衛尉), not the imperial clan court (宗正).

proposals.before: Cui Xuan as minister of justice called it rebellion; for years the case would not close.
proposals.after: Cui Xian as minister of justice called it rebellion; for years the case would not close.
proposals.reason: 崔暹 is Cui Xian; later units already use Cui Xian for the same person.

proposals.before: Cui Xuan was minister of justice and took it for rebellion; for years the case was not closed.
proposals.after: Cui Xian was minister of justice and took it for rebellion; for years the case was not closed.
proposals.reason: 崔暹 is Cui Xian; later units already use Cui Xian for the same person.

decisions.reason: s0034 has 汲郡, which is Ji commandery; Jiyin would be 濟陰. Replacing Jiyin with Ji commandery restores the place-name without other changes.
The literal likewise misread 汲郡 as Jiyin; Ji commandery's city matches the Chinese and leaves the rest of the sentence intact.
s0065 opens with 顯祖, the temple name Xianzu; Xianzong would be 顯宗. Emperor Xianzu corrects only that misreading.
The literal field repeats the same 顯祖→Xianzong error; Emperor Xianzu matches the Chinese temple name and preserves the rest of the wording.
s0112 names the father 文業; 業 is yè, so Wenye, not Wenyue. The proposed swap corrects only that given name.
Literal likewise mistook 文業 as Wenyue; Wenye is the accurate reading and leaves the rest of the sentence unchanged.
s0129 has 衛尉少卿, an office under the Court of the Guards (衛尉), not the Court of the Imperial Clan (宗正). Junior chamberlain for the palace guards restores the correct bureau.
The literal repeats the imperial-clan misidentification of 衛尉少卿; junior chamberlain for the palace guards matches 衛尉 and keeps the rest intact.
s0056 names 崔暹; 暹 is Xian, not Xuan. Cui Xian matches the Chinese and the preferred form used elsewhere for this person.
Literal likewise misread 暹 as Xuan; Cui Xian corrects the given name without altering the rest of the sentence.

claimRevisions.reason: Accepted r0003 shows English Emperor Xianzong came only from the bad translation of 顯祖; the title claim must read Emperor Xianzu while keeping zh, id, subject, predicate, certainty, and evidence.
Accepted r0005 shows English Wenyue came only from the bad translation of 文業; the personal-name claim must read Wenye while keeping zh, pinyin, id, subject, predicate, certainty, and evidence.
